whenRequired:
Fill this in before any AS 1851-2012 Section 6 test where the building is occupied and you will isolate the brigade signal, operate ancillary outputs, or sound the occupant warning — the monthly, six-monthly, annual and five-yearly routine service, a commissioning re-test, or fault-finding at a live panel.

WHY IT IS A SWMS AND NOT JUST A JSEA. A fire detection and alarm system is an essential service, and the installation, testing or maintenance of an essential service in relation to a structure is construction work under WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 289(2)(e). Opening and testing at a live FIP is work on or near energised electrical installations (s 291(k)); reaching detectors, sounders, beam and duct devices at ceiling height carries a fall of more than 2m (s 291(a)). Both are high risk construction work, so a SWMS is prepared before the work starts (s 299).

THE FOUR CONDITIONAL HRCW TRIGGERS — CHECK EACH ONE ON THIS SITE BEFORE YOU START.
• s 291(d) disturbance of asbestos — YES on any building built or refurbished before 2004 where you will lift a ceiling tile or enter a riser, plant room, ceiling void or roof space, unless the asbestos register says otherwise. Check the register first.
• s 291(f) work in or NEAR a confined space — YES wherever you work beside a lift pit, duct, plenum, tank or smoke reservoir. This SWMS does not cover ENTRY. Entry needs a permit, a standby, gas testing and the confined space SWMS.
• s 291(o) movement of powered mobile plant — YES in any warehouse, dock, carpark or plant room with forklifts, order pickers, delivery vehicles, scissor lifts or cleaning machines moving through a test area.
• s 291(p) artificial extremes of temperature — YES for detectors in cold stores, freezer rooms and chillers.
Tick the ones that apply on the site prompts and brief them at sign-on.

SIGN-ON, AND WHAT s 300 ACTUALLY SAYS. Every worker signs on to this SWMS before starting. That signature is Safe QLD's method of demonstrating the consultation required by WHS Act 2011 (Qld) ss 46–49 and the information, training and instruction required by WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 39, and it is part of the arrangements for ensuring the work is carried out in accordance with the SWMS that s 300 requires. s 300 itself is 'Compliance with safe work method statement': it requires the PCBU to put those arrangements in place and to stop the work immediately if it is not being carried out in accordance with the SWMS. It does not require a signature. Do not tell a worker the law makes them sign — tell them Safe QLD does, and why.

COPY TO THE PRINCIPAL CONTRACTOR. s 301 requires the SWMS to be given to the principal contractor only where the high risk construction work is carried out in connection with a CONSTRUCTION PROJECT, which s 292 defines as construction work costing $250,000 or more. A routine AS 1851 Section 6 service is almost never a construction project, so on most services there is no principal contractor and this duty does not arise. Do not go looking for one that does not exist.

FALLS — WHAT s 299(4) REQUIRES US TO WRITE DOWN. Because step 7 can fall back to a platform ladder (administrative) or to fall arrest (PPE), s 299(4) requires this SWMS to describe ALL the control measures considered, including by addressing the general fall protection requirements in s 79(3). Considered, in this order:
1. Telescopic test pole from floor level — ELIMINATES the fall. Used wherever the ceiling height and device type allow it, which is most heads in a commercial building.
2. Work from the ground or on a solid construction — a permanent walkway, catwalk, gantry or fixed platform with edge protection (s 78(3)). Used wherever the building provides one. Rejected only where none exists at that device.
3. Fall prevention device — EWP or mobile scaffold with guardrails (s 79(3)(a)). Used wherever pole reach fails and the floor will take the machine and access permits it. Rejected where the floor loading, doorway width, ceiling height, live tenancy or trading hours make it not reasonably practicable, and the reason is written on the job.
4. Work positioning system (s 79(3)(b)). Rarely applicable to detector testing in a commercial ceiling; rejected where there is no suitable structure to position from.
5. Platform ladder (administrative) or fall arrest (PPE, s 79(3)(c)) — LAST RESORT, only where 1 to 4 are all not reasonably practicable at that location, with the reason recorded device by device. Fall arrest is gated on the s 80 rescue plan: no written, tested rescue plan and no immediate means of rescue means nobody clips on.

Where the whole visit is a keypad check with nothing isolated, nothing sounded and nothing opened, that is testing or maintenance of a minor nature under s 289(3)(d) — a JSEA at the panel is enough.

STOP AND GET THE SWMS THAT COVERS IT if the job turns into: entry to a lift pit, duct, plenum, tank or smoke reservoir (confined space); ENERGISED ELECTRICAL WORK (this SWMS does not authorise it and does not meet Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 200 — a separate SWMS is required); disturbance of asbestos; any cutting, grinding or soldering (hot work); or a boom lift 11 m or over.
permits: Occupier's written authority to isolate the fire detection and alarm system, the ASE and every other system that signals through that ASE — naming the person holding the fire watch, the period of isolation and the MAXIMUM period the system may be off line before it is restored or the isolation is formally re-authorised in writing

ASE isolation reference from the fire monitoring centre, or the monitoring contractor's isolation request form where the isolation cannot be done at the panel — lodged ahead of the day, not on the morning

Gaseous / special hazard release lock-off permit — a separate, separately signed line for every gaseous, pre-action and deluge system on site: release isolated, actuator or solenoid disconnected, verified at the cylinder bank or valve by name and time, and signed back on at restoration. This is not folded into the general electrical isolation permit.

Asbestos register sighted before any ceiling tile is lifted or any riser, plant room, ceiling void or roof space is entered — a pre-start gate, recorded on the job. No register on a pre-2004 building means the space is treated as suspect and the device is marked untested.
Site contractor sign-in and permit to work
Electrical isolation permit / lock-out tag-out for the FIP 240 V fire supply, and for any lift, AHU, smoke control or shutter plant handed over by another trade

Roof access or working at height permit where the site requires one — and, where fall arrest may be used, the written rescue plan that WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 80 requires, on site before anyone clips on
Confined space entry permit — only if a device sits in a lift pit, duct, plenum, tank or smoke reservoir. If it does, stop and use the confined space SWMS, not this one.

Energised electrical work — NOT permitted under this SWMS. If the work genuinely cannot be done dead, stop: a separate safe work method statement with the contents prescribed by Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 200, plus the recorded risk assessment under s 199(1)(a) and the authorisation under s 199(1)(e), must be in place first.
Hot work permit — not required for this activity. If cutting, drilling that throws sparks, grinding or soldering is added to the scope, stop and get one (AS 1674.1:2025).
ppe: Hearing protectors to AS/NZS 1270, SELECTED UNDER AS/NZS 1269.3 AGAINST THE MEASURED LEVEL AT YOUR POSITION — not automatically the highest class. Level-dependent or communications-equipped protectors are the default on this job so the sounder, the panel and the stop word stay audible; over-protection is itself a hazard here. Carried on you and fitted before the first sounder is keyed.
Safety glasses to AS/NZS 1337.1 — worn whenever the panel door is open and at the battery bank
Insulated gloves rated for the panel supply voltage for work at the 240 V section and the battery set
General work gloves for ceiling tiles, cable trays, risers and break-glass element replacement
Safety footwear to AS 2210.3, enclosed, for plant rooms and risers
Long-sleeve hi-vis shirt with visible Safe QLD ID so occupants can see who is causing the noise
P2 disposable respirator for ceiling voids, risers and dusty plant rooms
Head torch — hands free, and a charged phone carried on you, not left at the panel
Hard hat where an EWP is used or work is going on overhead

Full body harness and lanyard to AS/NZS 1891.1, used under AS/NZS 1891.4 — LAST RESORT ONLY under WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 79(3)(c), and not used at all until the written rescue plan required by s 80 exists, has been tested, a means of rescue is on site and immediately available, and everyone involved is trained in it. Clipped to a rated anchor or the EWP basket anchor, never the handrail.
training: QBCC fire protection occupational licence covering install and maintain of fire alarm systems — the class that covers routine service and testing of fire detection and alarm systems
QBCC certify class for fire alarm systems where the technician is certifying the system, not just testing it

Queensland electrical work licence, or a restricted electrical licence covering the work, for anything on the 240 V side of the FIP — under the Electrical Safety Act 2002 (Qld) and the Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld)

Safety observer competence for anyone observing electrical work on or near energised electrical equipment (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 203(1)(c)) — a named role, not simply a second body in the room

Competence in rescue and resuscitation in accordance with recognised practices in the electricity industry, for every worker who performs or helps to perform electrical work (Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 211). Safe QLD's standard for this is low voltage rescue and CPR, current within 12 months.

Fall-arrest rescue competence for anyone who may use, or supervise the use of, a harness — the emergency and rescue procedure training required by WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 80(4). Nobody clips on unless a trained rescuer is on site.

Gaseous and special hazard suppression system competence for any technician testing detection in a protected space — how the release is isolated on that system type and how it is verified at the cylinder bank
Manufacturer or distributor competency for the panel type on site — Vigilant MX1/F4000, Pertronic F220, Ampac FireFinder, Kentec Taktis, Notifier
Work safely at heights (RIIWHS204E) where ladders, mobile scaffold, EWP or fall arrest are used
EWP operation — EWPA Yellow Card for a boom under 11 m, or a high risk work licence (WP) for a boom 11 m or over
Confined space entry and gas testing (RIIWHS202E) — only if entry is required; that work is not covered by this SWMS
Site induction and a walk-through of the building's fire and evacuation plan

This SWMS read and signed on by every worker before the job starts — Safe QLD's way of demonstrating the consultation required by WHS Act 2011 (Qld) ss 46–49 and the information, training and instruction required by WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 39, and part of the arrangements for compliance required by s 300

steps.step: 1. Book the test and get written authority to isolate — before the day, not at the panel
hazards: Unannounced test triggers a full building evacuation
Unintended brigade turnout and an unwanted alarm charge against the building owner
Test run over a critical occupancy — theatre, ICU, aged care, child care, data hall — with no arrangement in place
Wrong building, wrong panel, wrong ASE on a multi-panel campus
Audible portion pushed after hours and the crew quietly drops to one technician alone in an empty building

controls.control: Where an occupancy cannot take sounders at full volume in hours, the audible portion moves to after hours or to a one-zone-at-a-time test agreed with the facility manager in writing. Decide this before the day, not standing under a sounder.

No booking, no test. Confirmed in writing with the occupier at least 48 hours out: date, start and finish window, which zones, exactly how long the brigade signal will be off, and the maximum period it may be off before the system goes back on line.

Get the site's fire and evacuation plan (Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld), part 3), the last AS 1851 record of maintenance, the open defect list, and the site asbestos register. Read the ancillary cause-and-effect matrix and the special hazard (gaseous, pre-action, deluge) asset list before you arrive.

Occupier's written authority to isolate, naming: the detection system, the ASE, every other system that signals through that ASE, the named person who holds the fire watch, the period of isolation and the maximum isolation period. The occupier must have procedures giving protection equal to or better than the monitored system for the whole time it is isolated.

Confirm the attending technician holds a current QBCC fire protection occupational licence covering install and maintain of fire alarm systems, and that whoever signs the certification on the record of maintenance holds the certify class for fire alarm systems.

Confirm the panel identity before you touch it: address, panel designation, block plan and asset register all agree. On a multi-panel campus, photograph the panel label and match it to the job before isolating anything.

If the test moves after hours, the two-technician requirement is confirmed in writing before the day, together with: maximum shift hours, the interval since each technician's last shift, out-of-hours building access, lighting, lift availability and security, and confirmation that the fire watch and a contactable FM are physically present at night — not nominally rostered. After-hours work does not proceed as a one-technician job.

steps.responsible: Safe QLD supervisor, with the site facility manager

steps.step: 2. Sign in, brief the wardens, put the building on notice
hazards: Occupants self-evacuate on the first sounder
Wardens run a real evacuation on a test alarm
Another trade on hot work or a sprinkler impairment at the same time
Reception and floor wardens give occupants conflicting instructions once the phones start

controls.control: Face-to-face with the chief warden and reception before you touch anything: what will sound, in which zones, when, and the exact words reception uses when the phones start ringing.

Notices up at every affected floor and every lift lobby, and a PA announcement immediately before the first sounder test. Signage and announcements are administrative controls — they inform people, they do not stop anyone walking out.

One agreed stop word and one phone number. If the chief warden or the FM says stop, sounders go silent and the system goes back to normal before anything else is discussed. Both technicians carry the number; the technician away from the panel carries a radio or phone on an open channel so the stop word actually reaches them.
Check the site permit board: no hot work, no sprinkler impairment, no roof work under a smoke control fan while you are testing. If there is, the two jobs get sequenced, not run together.
Site PPE and visible Safe QLD ID on before you leave reception.

steps.responsible: Fire technician (lead), with the chief warden

steps.step: 3. Establish everything that signals through this ASE, isolate the brigade signal and log it
hazards: Unintended brigade turnout — appliances responding under lights and sirens to a test
Building left with no monitored path to the brigade and nobody watching it
Sprinkler flow and valve monitoring, hydrant and sprinkler pump alarms, gaseous release and fault signals and plant fault signals all silently unmonitored because they share the ASE
Isolation applied to the wrong panel or the wrong ASE
Isolation not recorded, so nobody knows it is on
Isolation runs long and nobody notices
A manual call point signals to the brigade because the detection isolate does not inhibit MCPs on this panel type

controls.control: Isolate at the FIP or ASE using the panel's own brigade-isolate function. Do not pull the ASE fuse and do not lift the line. Read the display back — 'ASE isolated' or 'brigade isolated' — before you do anything else.
Isolate zone by zone rather than whole-of-system wherever the panel supports it, so the unmonitored footprint is as small as the job allows.

Where the panel supports it, use a keyed isolate or lock the panel door with a lock whose only key you carry, so the isolate cannot be cleared or changed by anyone else while you are away from the panel.

Before you isolate, work out from the panel, the block plan and the cause-and-effect matrix exactly what signals through this ASE — detection, sprinkler flow and valve monitoring, hydrant and sprinkler pump alarm and fault, gaseous release and fault, lift and plant fault. Write that list into the occupier's written authority and into the fire watch's scope. The fire watch has to cover what is actually unmonitored, not just the detection zones.

Before you operate any manual call point, confirm on the panel type in front of you exactly what the isolate inhibits — MCPs, detection, or both — and prove it on the display before you press anything. If the isolate does not inhibit MCPs, isolate the MCP path separately or do not press one.

Ring the fire monitoring centre (Johnson Controls for QFD-monitored ASEs — confirm this site's centre on the job before you ring), give the site and account, and get a reference number. Where the panel cannot be isolated locally, the ASE isolation request form (QFD OM129) goes to the monitoring contractor ahead of the day, not on the morning.

Isolation tag on the panel door: date, time on, technician name, mobile, expected time off, MAXIMUM time off, and the fire watch's name. You put it on, and only you take it off. A tag tells people what is happening — it is a warning, not a lock.

Written in the site log book at the moment of isolation with the maximum isolation period stated, and a phone alarm set for the agreed off time and a second alarm for the maximum. If the work overruns, the system goes back on line, or the isolation is formally re-authorised in writing by the occupier before the maximum passes.

The occupier's fire watch starts the second the isolation goes on. You verify the named fire watch in person before the isolate goes on — you see them, you brief them on the area and on everything now unmonitored, and you confirm how they raise the alarm and call 000. Not by phone, not by assumption.

steps.step: 4. Lock off gaseous, pre-action and deluge release before any detector in a protected space is touched
hazards: Extinguishant discharged into an occupied data hall, comms room, switch room, UPS room, archive or generator room while people are inside
Oxygen depletion in a sealed room after discharge, and a space that cannot be re-entered
Pressure surge on discharge capable of blowing out room construction, ceilings and doors
Discharge noise loud enough to cause immediate hearing damage and to destroy hard drives
Pre-action or deluge sprinkler release actuated by the detection you are testing, putting water into a data hall or over a stage
A pyrotechnic actuator left connected while you believe the system is isolated
Manual release point operated by a passer-by who does not know the system is under test

controls.control: If a detector sits in a protected space and the release cannot be verified isolated at the cylinder bank or the release valve, it does not get tested today. Mark it untested with the reason and escalate. There is no version of this step where you test a detector on a live release.

Physically lock off the extinguishant release before anything in that space is tested: solenoid or actuator disconnected from the cylinder, or the release isolate applied and locked. VERIFY IT WITH YOUR OWN EYES AT THE CYLINDER BANK — the panel display is a second check, never the only one.
Confirm no pyrotechnic or squib actuator remains connected. If one is fitted and cannot be safely disconnected by you, the gaseous contractor does it or the space is not tested.
Pre-action and deluge release goes under the same regime: release valve isolated and verified at the valve, not on the display.
Cover or isolate the manual release point for the protected space and confirm it on the display.

Identify every special hazard system on site before you start — from the cause-and-effect matrix, the asset register and a walk of the cylinder rooms. A system you did not know about is the one that discharges.
Prove the release circuit reads isolated on the panel display and photograph the display before any detector in that space is operated.

Post the protected space at every door — 'suppression system isolated, fire system under test' — and brief anyone working in it face to face, including who to call and that the space has no automatic protection until you say so.

Restoration of every release circuit is a separate, separately ticked line on the step 11 restore checklist, re-proved at the cylinder bank and on the display, and re-verified before the fire watch stands down.

steps.responsible: Fire technician (lead), with the special hazard system contractor and the FM

steps.step: 5. Isolate ancillary outputs one at a time and put the panel in test
hazards: Lift recalled with a passenger in the car
Air handling shut down on a data hall, theatre or clean space
Smoke spill or stair pressurisation fan starting with someone on the roof or in the plant room
Door holders dropping a heavy fire door on a person, a trolley or an evacuation route
Fire or smoke shutter descending onto a person, a vehicle or a load, or sealing an evacuation route
Mag locks releasing on a secure area or failing secure on an exit

controls.control: Isolate each ancillary output individually against the site's cause-and-effect matrix (AS 1670.1:2024, or the edition the site was designed and commissioned to). Never assume a group isolate covers everything — prove each one on the display.
Lifts parked and out of service by the lift contractor or FM before any lift interface work. Cars checked empty by eye, out-of-service signage at every landing.

Fire and smoke shutters and roller shutters identified from the matrix and isolated individually. Drop path walked and cleared — nothing and nobody under the leaf, no pallet, no trolley, no vehicle. Nothing on the matrix gets a group isolate.
Roof and any plant room with a fan or damper on the matrix locked out by the trade that owns it before smoke control or pressurisation outputs are touched.
Where a door hold-open device is fitted, release and re-set it under control using the device itself; never wedge or prop a fire door as a substitute.
Where a plant space cannot be locked out, it is manned by a named person who stays there until the output work is finished — and you confirm they are there before you key anything.

Walk the door line before door holders release — nothing propped, nothing under the leaf, nobody in the swing. A pre-start visual check is administrative: it only works if you actually walk it, every time.

For a data hall or clean space where the FM will not wear a full AHU shutdown, prove the output at the interface relay instead, and write it on the report as an interface proved at the panel, not a functional shutdown — with the reason.

steps.responsible: Fire technician (lead), with the lift contractor and mechanical contractor

steps.step: 6. Work at the fire indicator panel — live supply and battery bank
hazards: 240 V supply and exposed terminals inside the panel
DC arc flash and burns from shorting a 24 V sealed lead-acid battery set — the short-circuit current is hundreds of amps
Hydrogen vented from sealed lead-acid cells under charge or fault inside a closed battery cabinet
Battery acid, and gas from a vented or swollen cell
Dropped tool bridging a terminal strip
Back and crush injury lifting battery sets out of a low cabinet
Panel put on battery when the mains is killed — the system is degrading from that moment, and a mains-fail fault will signal to the brigade if the ASE is not isolated

controls.control: Do everything you can from the keypad and the panel's test menu. Open to the mains section only for the work that genuinely cannot be done any other way.
Anything on the 240 V side is electrical work. De-energise at the panel's dedicated fire supply, lock it out with your own lock, tag it, and prove dead with a tested instrument before and after.

Working on or near energised electrical equipment ('near' means within 3 m of an exposed energised part — Electrical Safety Regulation 2026 (Qld) s 193) is permitted only in the circumstances in s 195(1): it is necessary in the interests of health and safety; it is necessary for the work to be performed properly; it is necessary for testing under s 196(1); or there is no reasonable alternative way of carrying out the work. If none of those apply, it gets done dead or it does not get done. THIS SWMS DOES NOT AUTHORISE ENERGISED ELECTRICAL WORK AND DOES NOT SATISFY ESR 2026 s 200 — a separate safe work method statement with the contents prescribed by s 200 must be prepared for it first.
Insulated terminal shrouds fitted to the battery bank and kept on except at the terminal being worked.
Open and ventilate the battery compartment before working at it. No ignition source at the cabinet, and no switching of load at the terminals inside a closed cabinet.

Before energised work starts: a competent person conducts AND RECORDS a risk assessment (ESR 2026 s 199(1)(a)); the separate s 200 SWMS is prepared (s 199(1)(b)); the work area and the isolation point are clear of obstructions (s 199(1)(c) and (d)); the isolation point is clearly marked or labelled and capable of being operated quickly (s 199(1)(d)); and the work is authorised after consulting the person with management or control of the workplace (s 199(1)(e)).

The energised work is observed by a SAFETY OBSERVER (ESR 2026 s 203(1)(c)) — a competent second person whose only job is to watch and to isolate and rescue. 'A second person present' is not a safety observer. The only exemption is s 203(3): the work consists only of testing AND the recorded risk assessment shows no serious risk. Only persons authorised for the work enter the immediate area (s 201).
Everyone performing or helping to perform electrical work is competent in rescue and resuscitation (ESR 2026 s 211). Keep the risk assessment and the s 200 SWMS as required by s 204.
Insulated tools only, and inspected before use.
Battery connection sequence: negative off first, negative on last. Nothing ever rested on top of a battery.
Rings, watch, metal lanyard and neck chain off before your hands go near the battery bank.

Before de-energising the FIP mains: confirm the ASE is isolated so the mains-fail fault does not signal, record the time the panel went onto battery, and set a maximum time on battery based on the battery capacity. The system is degrading the whole time it is off mains — if you hit the maximum, restore mains before continuing.
Battery sets over 16 kg — two-person lift or a trolley, one battery at a time, feet clear of the cabinet plinth. A swollen or leaking battery is not tested, it is replaced.
Safety glasses to AS/NZS 1337.1 and insulated gloves rated for the supply voltage on at the battery bank and whenever the panel door is open; sleeves down.

steps.responsible: Fire technician (lead); licensed electrical worker plus safety observer for any energised work

steps.step: 7. Test detectors, manual call points and beam, duct or aspirating devices
hazards: Fall of more than 2m from a ladder or step platform at ceiling height
Ladder set on a stair landing, a ramp or over a stairwell void
Contact with a live luminaire, busway or a sprinkler head while reaching
Hand or tool entering a duct or fan housing with the fan running
Asbestos-containing material disturbed by lifting a ceiling tile in a building built or refurbished before 2004
Test aerosol in the face of an occupant, particularly an asthmatic
Dust, insulation and vermin droppings from a ceiling void
Occupant, trolley or forklift moving through the work area under the ladder
Cuts from a broken break-glass element on manual call point reset

controls.control: Test from floor level with a telescopic test pole and smoke or heat cup wherever the ceiling allows it. Most heads in a commercial building never need a ladder.

Where the pole will not reach, work from the ground or from a solid construction — a permanent walkway, catwalk, gantry or fixed platform with edge protection — before any temporary access is considered (WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 78(3)).

Isolation under the work means a physical barricade a person cannot walk through — hard barriers or a closed-off aisle. In a warehouse or dock, get the aisle shut and the forklifts stopped in writing before you set up.

No hand and no tool enters a duct or fan housing until the mechanical contractor has isolated and locked out the fan and you have seen the lock and the stopped fan with your own eyes. Not a radio call, not an assurance.

Where the pole will not reach and there is no solid construction, an EWP or a mobile scaffold with guardrails — a fall prevention device under WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 79(3)(a) — before any ladder or harness is considered.

Where a hard barricade is genuinely not achievable, cones plus a posted spotter are the administrative fallback. Cones are not isolation and a spotter is not a barrier — if people or plant keep coming through, stop and get the area shut.

Ask the occupier for the site asbestos register BEFORE removing any ceiling tile or opening any ceiling void. The person with management or control of the workplace must keep it (WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 425) and must make it readily accessible to a PCBU that intends to carry out work at the workplace (s 427). If the register shows ACM in that space, or there is no register and the building was built or refurbished before 2004, do not disturb the material: mark the device untested with the reason and escalate to the supervisor.

Where a platform ladder is the only remaining option: AS 1892.1:2018 ladder, selected and used under AS 1892.5:2020, on level firm floor, three points of contact, never off the top two rungs, never on a stair landing, ramp or over a void. Record on the job why the pole, solid construction, EWP and scaffold were not reasonably practicable at that location — this is the record WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 299(4) requires.

Before operating any manual call point, confirm what the panel's isolate actually inhibits on this panel type and prove it on the display. Carry correct replacement break-glass elements; never reset a broken element bare-handed.
Test aerosol per the SDS — short bursts into the cup on the head. Not used over an occupied workstation without telling the people there, and not used in a food prep or clean area at all.
Work the zones in block plan order so every response can be matched device by device at the panel, and record each one as you go — not from memory afterwards.

Fall arrest is the LAST RESORT under WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 79(3)(c) — individual protection, used only where a fall prevention device and a work positioning system are both not reasonably practicable. Nobody clips on until ALL of the following exist: a written rescue plan for this location; a means of rescue on site and immediately available (EWP ground controls proven working, or a rescue kit with a trained operator present); the plan tested so it is effective; and everyone involved trained in it — WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 80. No rescue plan, no harness, no work at that device.
Harness and lanyard to AS/NZS 1891.1:2020, selected and used under AS/NZS 1891.4:2025, clipped to a rated anchor or the EWP basket anchor — never the handrail.
Glasses, gloves, P2 mask when a ceiling tile comes out, hard hat where an EWP or overhead work applies.

steps.step: 8. Sound the occupant warning at full volume — sounders, strobes and speakers
hazards: Sound pressure over 100 dB(A) at a metre from a sounder, with your head right under it, repeated all day
Hearing protection so heavy that the technician cannot hear the sounder, the panel or the agreed stop word
Strobes triggering a photosensitive epilepsy episode
Startle response in a hospital, aged care, child care ward, or beside moving machinery
Occupants with mobility, hearing or cognitive impairment distressed or put at risk by a test alarm
Occupants self-evacuating despite the notice

controls.control: Where AS 1851 lets the sound level be proved at the design point rather than under the device, measure at the design point and stand clear of the sounder.
One zone at a time rather than an all-of-building alarm, using the short-burst and silence functions so no sounder runs longer than the test needs.

Audibility verification is done by the second technician standing outside the high-level field, or by meter on a stand. Nobody stands under a sounder holding a meter for longer than the reading takes.

The exposure standard is L(Aeq,8h) 85 dB(A) and L(C,peak) 140 dB(C) — WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 56. Measure the level at the position you will actually stand, keep a running tally of minutes spent under sounders across the day, and stop when the tally says stop.

Audiometric testing is provided by Safe QLD for every technician required to wear hearing protection on this work — within 3 months of the worker commencing the work and at least every 2 years thereafter (WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 58).

The second technician keys the panel while you observe from clear of the device. Radio or phone link stays open between the panel and the technician in the field so the agreed stop word reaches whoever is under the sound.
Any area with a known photosensitive epilepsy risk is told before strobes run, and the FM gets the option to move those people out first.

From the site's fire and evacuation plan, identify persons with special needs in the affected zones before the sounders run — a person for whom it is reasonable to make different evacuation arrangements because of a characteristic of the person or their presence in the building (Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld) s 19). The FM and the chief warden decide whether those people are moved, individually briefed, or the zone is tested out of hours. You do not sound a zone until that decision is made.
If occupants start walking out: silence immediately, chief warden on the PA, system back to normal, then work out what to do next. Do not keep testing through a self-evacuation.

Hearing protectors to AS/NZS 1270 SELECTED UNDER AS/NZS 1269.3 AGAINST THE MEASURED LEVEL AT THE POSITION — not automatically the highest class. Over-protection is a hazard on this job: level-dependent or communications-equipped protectors are the default so speech, the panel and the stop word stay audible. Fitted before the first sounder is keyed, not after.

steps.step: 9. Prove the ancillary interfaces — lifts, AHU, smoke control, shutters, door holders
hazards: Lift recalling with a passenger or another trade in the car or shaft
Person trapped in a lift car when recall is proved
Smoke spill fan or pressurisation fan starting with hands inside the plant
Fire or smoke damper closing on a limb or a tool
Fire or smoke shutter descending onto a person, a trolley or a vehicle, or sealing an evacuation route
Heavy fire door released onto a person
Pre-action or deluge release actuated while proving a detection interface
Fail-safe exit door releasing and then not re-securing, leaving the building open

controls.control: The plant is under the control of the trade that owns it before you prove anything — lift contractor for lifts, mechanical contractor for AHU, smoke control and shutters. Their isolation goes on before yours comes off.

Nobody inside a fan housing, duct, damper, shutter drop path or lift shaft when an output is proved, and no lift car occupied. Look with your own eyes before you key it — do not take a radio call as proof.
Gaseous, pre-action and deluge release stays locked off and verified at the cylinder bank or valve for the whole of this step, exactly as set up in step 4.
Prove one output at a time, watch the plant actually respond, and reset it before moving to the next. Do not run a whole-building cause and effect in one hit on an occupied site.
Shutters proved one at a time with the drop path physically barricaded, and each shutter reset and proved back up before the next one is dropped.
Call and response with the person watching the far end before every output: 'proving lift 2 recall now — are you clear?' and wait for the answer. No answer, no output.
Every fail-safe exit door proved to release and proved to re-secure, then physically pushed on the walk-off before you leave that floor.
Record what the plant actually did against the cause-and-effect matrix, not what it was supposed to do.

steps.responsible: Fire technician (lead), with the lift and mechanical contractors

steps.step: 10. Working alone in plant rooms, risers, ceiling voids and on the roof
hazards: Nobody knows where you are or when you were last seen
Collapse, electric shock, heat stress or a fall behind a closed plant room door
Being locked in when a self-latching door closes behind you
Heat in a Queensland roof space or riser
Fragile roof sheeting and unguarded roof edges
Asbestos-containing material in risers, plant rooms, roof spaces and ceiling voids of pre-2004 buildings
Snakes, wasps and vermin in risers and roof spaces
A device turning out to be inside a lift pit, duct or plenum — an unplanned confined space
Fatigue on an after-hours test, and the two-technician rule quietly becoming one

controls.control: First ask whether the space has to be entered at all. If the device can be tested from outside the space, do that. If it cannot, and the space cannot be entered safely today, mark it untested with the reason and move on — an untested device on a report is recoverable, a technician down behind a locked door is not.

Two technicians for any plant room, riser, roof or ceiling-void work. Two people does not eliminate collapse, shock, heat or falls — it means somebody raises the alarm. It is a standing rule, not a resourcing call to make on the day at the van, and it holds absolutely for after-hours work.

Carry the key on your body. Before the door closes behind you, prove it opens from the inside. If it does not open from the inside, do not enter alone, regardless of resourcing. NEVER wedge or prop a fire-rated door: propping a fire door defeats compartmentation, and doing it while the detection system is isolated is indefensible. If a door must be held open, use a device that does not defeat the fire door and remove it on the way out.

Remote or isolated work — WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) s 48 requires a system of work that includes effective communication with the worker; it prescribes no interval. Safe QLD's system is a check-in every 30 minutes to the office or the second technician, with a written escalation if one is missed: FM rings the plant room, then attends, then rings 000.

Ask for the site asbestos register before entering any riser, plant room, ceiling void or roof space (WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) ss 425 and 427). If it shows ACM in the space, or there is no register and the building was built or refurbished before 2004, do not disturb anything: mark the device untested with the reason and escalate.

Roof access only through the permanent access and along the walkway. No stepping on unsupported sheeting, nothing on a roof in a storm or on wet sheeting, no work near an unguarded edge without restraint and the step 7 rescue-plan gate satisfied.
Heat: water in before you go up, roof spaces and risers done early in the day, out at the first headache or nausea and tell someone. Nobody works a roof space alone in the afternoon in summer.

On an after-hours test: maximum shift hours and minimum break since the last shift are set before the day, lighting and access are proved on arrival, and the fire watch and a contactable FM are physically on site. If any of that is missing when you get there, the audible portion does not run.

If a device is inside a lift pit, duct, plenum, tank or smoke reservoir — stop. That is a confined space under AS/NZS 2865 and the Confined spaces Code of Practice 2021 (Qld). It needs a permit, an entry standby, gas testing and a different SWMS. Mark it untested and move on.
Head torch, long sleeves, gloves, enclosed boots, and a charged phone on your body.

steps.step: 11. Restore the system and prove it back — the step nobody is allowed to rush
hazards: System or a single zone left in isolate overnight
Gaseous, pre-action or deluge release circuit left locked off, so the protected space has no suppression
Ancillary left isolated so lifts do not recall, shutters do not drop or AHU does not trip in a real fire
Brigade signal never restored — the building looks protected and is not
Sprinkler, hydrant pump or plant fault signalling left off with the ASE
Batteries left disconnected or panel left in test mode
Restoration done from memory at 4:55 pm

controls.control: The panel itself is the check that does not depend on anyone remembering. A fire indicator panel will not present as normal while an isolation, a fault or test mode stands — the common fault or isolate indication and the buzzer are designed into the equipment for exactly this moment. DO NOT SILENCE THE BUZZER TO MAKE THE PANEL LOOK NORMAL. The buzzer going quiet on its own, and the display clearing on its own, is the proof.

The restore checklist is worked top to bottom at the panel and read out loud with the second technician before anyone picks up a bag. It is a written checklist — an administrative control — so it only works if it is actually read. It is built into the Safe QLD job on the tablet: the job will not close and the report will not generate until every line is ticked and the monitoring centre's restore reference is entered. Annexure A to this SWMS is the same list on paper for when the tablet is flat. The list, item by item: brigade isolate off and confirmed received by the monitoring centre; every zone isolate cleared; every gaseous, pre-action and deluge release circuit restored, re-proved at the cylinder bank or valve and on the display; every other signal that shares the ASE proved back — sprinkler flow and valve, hydrant and sprinkler pump alarm and fault, plant fault; every ancillary output de-isolated and listed individually; MCP path restored; test mode exited; batteries connected and on charge and the panel back on mains; panel reading normal; tag removed.

The panel display must read normal — no isolate, no fault, no test-mode indication — and you photograph it as it reads, with the time visible. A photograph is a record, not a control: the control is that nobody leaves until the display actually reads normal.

Ring the monitoring centre, come off isolation against the same reference number you opened, then send one test signal and have them confirm receipt out loud. Isolation is not off until they say they got the signal.
Every ancillary de-isolated and one representative output re-proved live: one lift recalls, one AHU trips, one shutter drops and resets, the door holders release and reset.

Log book closed out with the time off isolation and your name, and the fire watch formally stood down in writing by the person who started it — after, not before, the monitoring centre confirms the signal.
You remove your own isolation tag and your own lock. Nobody else touches them, and they do not come off until everything above is done.

steps.responsible: Fire technician (lead), with the site facility manager

steps.step: 12. Records, defects and handover before you leave site
hazards: A critical defect found and not notified inside the legal deadline
Occupier signs an occupier statement that is not true
System left unable to detect or warn with nobody told
Results written up the next day from memory
Untested devices reported as tested

controls.control: The tablet will not generate the record of maintenance until every device on the register has a result, and it will not accept 'untested' without a written reason. It is still a procedural gate, not a physical one — if the tablet is down, the paper register gets the same discipline, device by device, at the panel.
Results entered device by device at the panel as you test.

A critical defect goes to the occupier in the approved form WITHIN 24 HOURS AFTER YOU CARRY OUT THE MAINTENANCE — not 24 hours after you notice it (Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld) s 53). A defect is a critical defect if it is likely to render the installation inoperable AND is reasonably likely to have a significant adverse impact on the safety of occupants if a fire or hazardous materials emergency happens (s 49) — and the regulation's own worked example of a critical defect is a defect making a fire detection and alarm system inoperable. That is a legal deadline with a penalty attached, not a courtesy.

Where a defect leaves the system unable to detect or warn, it is handed to the FM face to face before you leave, and the fire watch stays on until it is repaired. Tell them the occupier must have the repair carried out or corrective action taken no later than 1 month after the maintenance was carried out (Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld) s 54(4)).

Record of maintenance completed under AS 1851-2012 and left with the occupier. It must state the installation, the name and licence number of the appropriately qualified person, the maintenance date, what was done, that it complied with QDC part MP6.1, and the results including any repair or corrective action required — and it must include a statement SIGNED BY THE PERSON WHO CARRIED OUT THE MAINTENANCE certifying those matters are correct (Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld) s 55). Any critical defect notice given goes with it.

The occupier statement is the occupier's to prepare and sign, not yours (Building Fire Safety Regulation 2008 (Qld) s 55A). They must give the commissioner a copy within 10 business days of when they are required to prepare it — which is why your facts have to be right and on time. You supply the facts; you do not sign it for them.

Anything you could not test — an AHU the FM would not let you shut down, a detector in a space whose suppression could not be verified isolated, a locked tenancy, a device in a confined space, a ceiling void with ACM — goes on the report as untested with the reason, in plain words.

emergency:
REAL FIRE WHILE THE SYSTEM IS ISOLATED. Do not silence it. Take the ASE off isolate immediately so the signal goes through, run the panel's evacuate function, tell the chief warden, and ring 000 yourself — say clearly that the panel was under test and the brigade signal was isolated until this moment, and name any space whose suppression is locked off. Then stand at the FIP with the keys, the block plan and the zone in alarm, and hand it to the first officer in.

ACCIDENTAL DISCHARGE OF A GASEOUS OR SPECIAL HAZARD SYSTEM. Get everyone out of the space immediately and do not re-enter — the atmosphere may not support life and the noise alone can injure. Close the door, account for everyone by name, and ring 000 if anyone was inside or is unaccounted for. The space stays shut until it has been mechanically ventilated and cleared by the gaseous contractor or the brigade. Tell the FM and the Safe QLD supervisor before you do anything else on site, and do not restore or reset the system.

UNINTENDED BRIGADE TURNOUT. Do not reset the panel. Ring 000 and the fire monitoring centre straight away: technician test in progress, site address, panel location, ASE reference. Stay at the FIP — the crew want the panel, not a phone call, and the panel history has to be intact when they arrive. Tell the Safe QLD supervisor the same day so the owner can answer the unwanted alarm charge: a charge for the service is payable by the person for whose benefit it was provided under the Fire Services Act 1990 (Qld), chapter 4A, part 6 (Charges for services), and the current amount is in the QFD schedule of charges for the current financial year. Giving a false alarm of fire is also an offence (Fire Services Act 1990 (Qld) s 150B) — say plainly that it was a test.

BUILDING SELF-EVACUATES ON A TEST. Silence the sounders, get the chief warden on the PA to say it was a test, restore the system to normal, and let the wardens run the return. You do not call people back into a building.

YOU CANNOT RESTORE THE SYSTEM. It does not get left isolated and walked away from. The fire watch stays on and its scope covers everything still unmonitored, any locked-off suppression is named in writing to the FM, the FM is told in person, the Safe QLD supervisor is told before you leave site, and the after-hours number is left with the FM in writing.

ELECTRIC SHOCK AT THE PANEL. Do not touch the person. Kill the supply at the fire supply isolator, then ring 000 and start CPR if needed. The panel stays isolated and tagged out and nothing is disturbed. An electric shock is a notifiable incident — ring Workplace Health and Safety Queensland and the Electrical Safety Office on 1300 362 128, and the site must be preserved (Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (Qld), part 3; and the notification duties under the Electrical Safety Act 2002 (Qld)).

FALL OR INJURY AT HEIGHT. Do not move them unless they are in further danger. Ring 000, and put someone in the lift lobby to walk the ambulance to the right level — crews lose minutes in big buildings. If someone is suspended in a harness, run the written rescue plan for that location NOW: it is time-critical, get their weight off the leg straps and get them down. If there was no rescue plan, they should not have been clipped on.

HEAT ILLNESS IN A ROOF SPACE OR RISER. Out, into airconditioning, fluids, and ring the supervisor. If they are confused or have stopped sweating, ring 000 — that is heat stroke.

Before you start, read the site's fire and evacuation plan for the first aid kit, the defib, the muster point and the nearest hospital. Not after.

siteSpecificPrompts: Which FIP, where is it, who holds the key, and is there more than one panel or a sub-panel network on this site? Photograph the panel label and match it to the job before you isolate.
Where is the ASE, and can the brigade signal be isolated at the panel — or does this site need an isolation request to the monitoring contractor first?

What else signals through this ASE besides detection — sprinkler flow and valve monitoring, hydrant or sprinkler pump alarm and fault, gaseous release and fault, lift and plant fault? List it, put it in the written authority, and give it to the fire watch.
Monitoring centre phone number and this site's account / ASE reference — write it on the tablet before you isolate.

Is there any gaseous, special hazard, pre-action or deluge system on this site? Which rooms does it protect, where is the cylinder bank or release valve, who is the contractor, and how is the release physically locked off and verified?
Where are the manual release points for those protected spaces, and how are they covered or isolated?
Who is the chief warden today and what is their mobile? Who is on reception when the phones start ringing?
Who is the named fire watch while the system is isolated, what area do they cover, what is now unmonitored, and how do they raise the alarm? Have you seen them in person?
Agreed isolation-off time, MAXIMUM isolation period, and who rings whom if it is going to slip?
On this panel type, does the detection isolate inhibit manual call points as well? Prove it on the display before you press one.

Is there a current asbestos register for this building, and does it show ACM in any ceiling void, riser, plant room or roof space you need to enter? If there is no register and the building predates 2004, what is your plan?
